newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ruling coalition starts oil price meeting.
newsitem.headline: India's ruling coalition starts oil price meeting.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition on Sunday began a meeting to discuss the possibility of raising the domestic prices of some petrloeum products.
Alliance officials said the front would also discuss a controversial bill to reserve one third of the seats in the lower house and state assemblies for women would also be discussed.
The bill has split Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party.

Representatives of the alliance's 15 parties began the closed-door meeting at 3.30 p.m. (1000 GMT). Information Minister Jaipal Reddy was scheduled to address a news conference at about 6.30 p.m (1300 GMT)
Gujral, who holds the petroleum ministry portfolio, and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram attended the crucial meeting.
It was widely expected that Gujral's centre-left coalition would recommend raising the prices of some oil products to plug a ballooning subsidy bill.

Newspapers this week said the government had tentatively decided to raise the prices of diesel and kerosene with a plan that would trim about $1.5 billion from the subsidy bill but spare petrol users.

Under the plan, kerosene prices would be increased by 20 percent, while those of high speed diesel and liquified petroleum gas (LPG) would be raised by 15 percent. The price of petrol, which is not subsidised, would remain unchanged.
On Saturday, the Confederation of Indian Industry said the prices of high-speed diesel, LPG and kerosene should be increased immediately by 15 percent.
It also called for the phasing out of subsidies on those three petroleum products within two to three years.

But left-wing parties in the United Front were opposed to raising prices, and instead favoured increasing production, cutting import duties on crude oil and petroleum products and discouraging the use of luxury cars.
